programs.title: Frontrunners
programs.desc: . Social entrepreneur Doya Yuto supports Ghana through his fashion brand and NPO. By providing fair wages and reinvesting profits, he builds schools and expands education in disadvantaged communities.

programs.title: Asia Insight
programs.desc: , Episode 2, Season 14. With nearly 15,000 cases a year, Indonesia has the third most cases of leprosy in the world. We meet survivors working to support patients and fight discrimination. Vinay Murthy, Naoki Nomura, Haruo Sakitsu.

programs.title: Newsroom Tokyo
programs.desc: . This program gives you comprehensive coverage of events in Japan and Asia. It explains the day's developments and what is behind them. Yuko Fukushima, Aiko Doden, Takafumi Terui, Shoichiro Beppu, Hideki Nakayama, Takuma Yoshioka, Koichiro Tanaka, Chan-ju Kim, Abhishek Dhulia, Aki Shibuya.

programs.title: Direct Talk
programs.desc: , Episode 248. Ito Satomi has designed costumes for many top-tier figure skaters from Japan and overseas. She shares her passion and inspiration for her craft. Gene Otani.

programs.title: IMPACTS: Climates Change the World
programs.desc: . The entire Earth is affected by climate change, occurring with a greater speed and scale than ever before. This program uses scientific data and the latest findings to raise awareness on its impact.

programs.title: Ukiyoe EDO-LIFE: Bustling Scenes of Old Tokyo
programs.desc: , Episode 14, Season 2. For a time during the Edo period, fireworks lit up the skies practically every night in the summer. It was a chance for women to dress up and let loose ... and grab the attention of male suitors.

programs.title: Medical Frontiers
programs.desc: . Biologic drugs, made mainly from antibodies, have transformed the approach to treating chronic inflammatory diseases such as asthma and rheumatoid arthritis. We explore their mechanisms and potential. Erica Angyal, Maxwell Powers.

programs.title: Voices of the Blind Songstresses
programs.desc: In Japan, "goze" were blind female travelling performers. We look at the lives of those songstresses who, shamisen in hand, travelled throughout Japan, singing their songs to earn a living.
